chunk_findings.detail: `_stranded_lines` interpolates each element of `r["stranded"]` verbatim (`f"  [!] {t}"` for `t in r["stranded"]`), i.e. it assumes the status dict carries plain strings, exactly like `_health_lines` does for `r["health"]`. But the change's own test (`tests/test_removed_item_lease.py::test_status_lists_the_stranded_item_in_both_clones`) asserts that the very same field, read back from `ddflow --json status`, is a list of *dicts*: `rows = json.loads(out)["stranded"]`, `[r["item"] for r in rows]`, `rows[0]["holder"]`, `rows[0]["text"]`. Since the human and `--json` surfaces are fed by the same status dict produced by `ddflow/api/reporting/overview.py` (the other accessors in `_print_status` — `r["ready"]`, `r["waiting"]`, `r["health"]` — are likewise the shared dict), the two shapes cannot both be right. With the JSON shape the human line prints a raw Python representation of the dict, e.g. `  [!] {'item': 'T2', 'holder': 'alice', 'text': '...'}`, instead of the message that `stranded_text` produced; the test does not catch it because it only checks for the substrings `"Removed, lease still held"` and `"T2"`, both of which survive inside the dict repr. The line should render `t["text"]` (or the status builder should store strings), otherwise `ddflow status` shows internal structure to the user in both clones, including the holder's clone where the intended `ddflow release T2` remedy is buried in a dict dump.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `mine` argument is fetched as `log.clone_id(create=False)` and passed to `stranded_text`, but `_require` still calls `stranded_text` with `ls.clone` and `mine` in `stranded_text(item, ..., ls.clone, mine)`. The remainder of the change (cleanup.py) is the only place that defines the new `stranded_text` signature and the remedy decision. This part does not answer the previously reported `_stranded_lines`/dict-vs-text defect, because it does not touch `ddflow/surfaces/commands/reporting.py` at all; the manifest still shows that file only adding `_stranded_lines`, while the change’s own test (`tests/test_removed_item_lease.py::test_status_lists_the_stranded_item_in_both_clones`) reads the `stranded` status field as a list of dicts. If `_stranded_lines` still interpolates each element verbatim as a string in the strain shown in the prior finding, that test fails on the exact new behavior this change claims to add.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/_common.py:29 (`_require`)

chunk_findings.detail: The function's docstring promises "the remedy is never one this clone would refuse", but that promise is not kept when `mine` is `None`. For example, in a clone with no clone id set (`log.clone_id(create=False)` returns `None`), if a removed item's lease is held by another clone, `stranded_text` receives `clone` non-empty but `mine=None`. The condition `clone and mine is not None and clone != mine` is false, so it falls through to the generic fix starting with `ddflow release <item>`. In that clone, `release` refuses because the lease is held by another clone, so the status/wait/merge/complete/heartbeat message advises a command that will be refused, contrary to the intent and docstring.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/cleanup.py:stranded_text

chunk_findings.detail: The previous finding still holds: `_stranded_lines` interpolates each element of `r["stranded"]` verbatim with `f"  [!] {t}"`, but the status field is a list of **dicts**, as the change's own JSON test requires (`rows[0]["item"]`, `rows[0]["holder"]`, `rows[0]["text"]`). Input: after Bob removes `T2` and Alice's live lease is present, JSON status has `{"stranded": [{"item": "T2", "holder": "alice", "text": "ddflow release T2"}]}`. Text `ddflow status` then renders `[!] {'item': 'T2', 'holder': 'alice', 'text': 'ddflow release T2'}` instead of the intended item-plus-message line. The added text-status assertion does not answer this because the raw dict repr also contains `"T2"`.

The remainder of the change (cleanup.py) is the only place that defines the new `stranded_text` signature and the remedy decision. This part does not answer the previously reported `_stranded_lines`/dict-vs-text defect, because it does not touch `ddflow/surfaces/commands/reporting.py` at all; the manifest still shows that file only adding `_stranded_lines`, while the change’s own test (`tests/test_removed_item_lease.py::test_status_lists_the_stranded_item_in_both_clones`) reads the `stranded` status field as a list of dicts. If `_stranded_lines` still interpolates each element verbatim as a string in the strain shown in the prior finding, that test fails on the exact new behavior this change claims to add.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/_common.py:29 (`_require`)

chunk_findings.detail: The function's docstring promises "the remedy is never one this clone would refuse", but that promise is not kept when `mine` is `None`. For example, in a clone with no clone id set (`log.clone_id(create=False)` returns `None`), if a removed item's lease is held by another clone, `stranded_text` receives `clone` non-empty but `mine=None`. The condition `clone and mine is not None and clone != mine` is false, so it falls through to the generic fix starting with `ddflow release <item>`. In that clone, `release` refuses because the lease is held by another clone, so the status/wait/merge/complete/heartbeat message advises a command that will be refused, contrary to the intent and docstring.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/cleanup.py:stranded_text

chunk_findings.detail: The previous finding still holds: `_stranded_lines` interpolates each element of `r["stranded"]` verbatim with `f"  [!] {t}"`, but the status field is a list of **dicts**, as the change's own JSON test requires (`rows[0]["item"]`, `rows[0]["holder"]`, `rows[0]["text"]`). Input: after Bob removes `T2` and Alice's live lease is present, JSON status has `{"stranded": [{"item": "T2", "holder": "alice", "text": "ddflow release T2"}]}`. Text `ddflow status` then renders `[!] {'item': 'T2', 'holder': 'alice', 'text': 'ddflow release T2'}` instead of the intended item-plus-message line. The added text-status assertion does not answer this because the raw dict repr also contains `"T2"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/reporting.py:_stranded_lines

chunk_findings.detail: The text-status assertion is vacuous for the renderer defect: it only checks `"T2" in text + err`. Since the broken `_stranded_lines` prints the entire dict repr `{'item': 'T2', ...}`, that substring is present, so the test passes equally for the buggy raw-dict rendering and the intended formatted line. It should assert the rendered line uses `rows[0]["item"]`/`rows[0]["text"]` and does not print a Python dict repr.
